subject: Deployment path comparison & TCO request — Hosted / Dedicated / Private
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia@nimblemetrics.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated for Nimble Metrics — usage detail

Thanks again for the quick demo earlier today. Two quick follow-ups from our side as we evaluate deployment paths:

1) I've attached our Q1 usage snapshot (nimble_metrics_usage_report_Q1.csv) — you'll see average tokens/day and a few burst events.
2) Key asks: a simple TCO sketch comparing (a) Hosted API per-token with caching heuristics, (b) Dedicated reserved capacity with a 12-month commit, and (c) Private VPC (rough on-prem estimate). Please include assumptions about KV cache hit rates and batched vs single-request latencies.

Goal: pick a pilot deployment within the next 6 weeks. Our constraints: 99th pct latency target ~200ms for short chat flows, PII redaction with in-flight processing okay, and EU data will be small initially.

Thanks — can you confirm what baseline inputs you need (peak RPS, avg tokens, retention)?

— Lydia
CTO, Nimble Metrics

Attachment: nimble_metrics_usage_report_Q1.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated for Nimble Metrics — usage detail

Lydia — thanks for the data and the clear asks. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next step plan.

Recap (from today's call + the Q1 file):
- Avg tokens/day (Q1): ~42M tokens/day; 95th percentile hourly spikes ~2.3M tokens.
- Peak concurrency: you mentioned brief spikes toward 180 rps for short chat flows.
- Latency target: 99th ~200ms for small-turn interactions (we should confirm if that includes network egress).
- Data: mostly US; small EU footprint for regulatory routing later.

Initial TCO approach (high level):
- Hosted API (per-token): good for fast pilot; we model per-token + caching. With a 60% effective KV/prefix cache hit on reuseable prompts and batching of ephemeral requests we expect ~35–40% lower billed tokens on normalized traffic. Best when you want no infra ops.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): better unit economics at steady sustained throughput. For your baseline, a 12-month reserved commit with autoscale headroom would reduce per-token equivalent cost by ~22–30% vs hosted at current pricing assumptions, but requires a commit baseline (we model a 60% commit of sustained Q1 avg).
- Private VPC / On‑prem: highest control for data residency and auditability; expected engineering lift and setup (~8–12 weeks) plus hardware procurement/ops. For your token volume, on‑prem amortized over 3 years can be competitive if you can sustain >70% utilization.

I've attached a first pass pricing workbook (redwood_pricing_v2.xlsx) with assumptions and sensitivity knobs (cache hit, batch size, reserved commit %).

Open items we need from you to finalize an apples-to-apples TCO:
- Confirm typical tokens per request (median + 95th) and breakdown by long vs short flows.
- Clarify acceptable fallback policy during spikes (e.g., degrade to smaller model / increase batch latency).
- Any procurement or security PO constraints that push you away from hosted?

Recommended next step: we prepare a 2‑page TCO sensitivity matrix + a short decision memo for your procurement team. Can we set a 30–40 minute follow-up next week? I can also run a short sim that shows cost at different cache-hit and commit levels.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_pricing_v2.xlsx (Excel, 112KB)

Thanks Karthik — workbook received and I skimmed the assumptions. A few clarifications before we take this to procurement:

- Tokens per request: median ~120 tokens, 95th ~1,800 (these are mixed chat/summary workloads).
- Cacheability: roughly 40–55% of requests should benefit from prefix caching (depends on our autocomplete flows).
- Peak expectations: bursts to ~200 rps for ~5–10 minutes, sustained peak periods during business hours of ~90–110 rps.
- Security/procurement: hosted is preferred for speed but procurement will request SOC2 evidence + a standard MSA. Private VPC is on the table if the procurement timeline aligns (they've budgeted for a Q3 rollout if we can show reason).

Can you include in the TCO: an explicit row for "reserve commit sensitivity" (show impact at 40%, 60%, 80% commit of sustained avg), and a row modeling KV cache hit at 30%, 50%, 70%. Also show a simple 3-year amortized on-prem column with conservative hardware pricing.

We can do a 30 min follow-up on Tue 5/4 9–9:30 PT — does that work?

— Lydia
